Main.sentence: Chicago Lawn is one of the 77 ___E:community areas of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago)___ , Illinois.

It is located on the southwest side of the city. Its community neighbors include ___E:Gage Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_Park,_Chicago)___ , ___E:West Englewood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Englewood,_Chicago)___ , ___E:Ashburn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Chicago)___ , and ___E:West Lawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Lawn,_Chicago)___ .

It is bounded by the ___E:CSX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CSX)___ and ___E:Norfolk Southern Railway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Southern_Railway)___ tracks on the east, Central Park Avenue on the west, 59th Street on the north, and the ___E:Belt Railway of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belt_Railway_of_Chicago)___ on the south, and is 13 km (8.1 mi) southwest of the ___E:Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop)___ .
Local citizens refer to the area as " Marquette Park ," after the ___E:park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_Park_(Chicago))___ in its center.
The city of Chicago Lawn was founded by John F. Eberhart in 1871. Although it was annexed by the city of Chicago in 1889, it remained mostly farmland with some scattered settlements until the 1920s.

Between 1920 and 1930 the population increased from 14,000 to 47,000. Residents of ___E:German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany)___ and ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland)___ descent began to move into the area from the ___E:Back of the Yards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_of_the_Yards#Back_of_the_Yards)___ and ___E:Englewood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Englewood,_Chicago)___ neighborhoods. ___E:Poles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland)___ , ___E:Bohemians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemia)___ , and ___E:Lithuanians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania)___ followed them. Most new residents belonged to various Protestant denominations, but Chicago Lawn also was home to many Roman Catholic churches and schools.
Today, there are six Catholic institutions that make up the Marquette Park Catholic Campus Council.

Chicago Lawn was a thriving urban neighborhood as the ___E:Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ hit the nation and by 1940 its population had reached 49,291. In 1941, the ___E:National Biscuit Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabisco)___ announced plans to build a huge bakery in Chicago Lawn. When completed, this was the largest bakery in one location in the world.
The size of the facility was doubled in the late 1990s.

The ___E:Lithuanian community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanians_in_Chicago)___ has maintained a notable presence in the area by establishing a network of institutions that earned their community the label as the Lithuanian Gold Coast .

They formed some of the richest savings and loans in the city. The ___E:Lithuanian Sisters of Saint Casimir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisters_of_Saint_Casimir)___ founded ___E:Holy Cross Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Cross_Hospital_(Chicago))___ in 1928 and ___E:Maria High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_High_School_(Chicago,_Illinois))___ in 1952 (originally established as St. Casimir Academy in 1911).
The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary Church was established in 1927 on the corner of 69th Street and Washtenaw Avenue.

It was founded as a Lithuanian ___E:national parish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_parish)___ and services are still held in ___E:Lithuanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_language)___ .

An ___E:Art Deco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco)___ monument was erected by Chicago's ___E:Lithuanian community U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanians_in_Chicago)___ in ___E:Marquette Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquette_Park_(Chicago))___ commemorating Lithuanian pilots ___E:Stasys Girėnas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stasys_Gir%C4%97nas)___ and ___E:Steponas Darius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steponas_Darius)___ who died in the crash of the ___E:Lituanica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lituanica)___ in 1933.

Chicago's changing racial demographics had a profound impact on Chicago Lawn. In the 1960s many of the white Americans had fled Englewood & West Englewood and Chicago Lawn became a target for civil rights groups' open housing marches during the ___E:Civil Rights Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Movement)___ .

In 1966, as part of the ___E:Chicago Freedom Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Freedom_Movement)___ , ___E:Martin Luther King Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr.)___ led a march into Marquette Park, where the marchers met a violent reaction.

King himself was hit by a rock. Violence also erupted in the neighborhood when ___E:Gage Park High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gage_Park_High_School)___ attempted to integrate after Brown v. Board of Education (1954).

However, over the next decade the racial composition of the neighborhood changed radically and by the ___E:2000 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census)___ ___E:African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_Americans)___ had become the largest racial group comprising 53% of the population, with ___E:Hispanic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans)___ and Non-Hispanic whites groups accounting for 35% and 10% respectively.
There are also ___E:Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews)___ and ___E:Palestinian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region))___ communities in the neighborhood.

Some Irish, Poles, and Lithuanians still remain too, although most have moved further south and west. Many of the Lithuanians and Poles have reestablished their communities in ___E:Lemont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemont,_Illinois)___ .
By the 1920s Arabs immigrated to Chicago, and political turmoil in the decades following the 1948 creation of Israel brought more Palestinian Muslims to Chicago.
Arab families live in Chicago Lawn and Gage Park Neighborhoods.
Arab community founded Chicago Islamic Center and Mosque on 63rd.

Many Middle Eastern store and restaurant near Mosque area. Arab families come from ___E:Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_(region))___ , ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ , ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ , and ___E:Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon)___ .

In the 1950s, ___E:Palestinians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians)___ with families moved out of their boardinghouses and shops and into apartments and homes just west of Chicago's "Black Belt." By the 1970s, they formed a concentrated residential community in Gage Park and Chicago Lawn, on the South Side, and had established a business district with stores catering to Arab clientele.
Arab community founded Chicago Islamic Center and Mosque on 63rd.
Many Middle Eastern store and restaurant near the Mosque area. Chicago's largest concentration of Palestinians still lives in these areas and in the communities to the south and west of them.
___E:Chicago Public Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Public_Schools)___ operates public schools in the neighborhood.
The ___E:Chicago Public Library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Public_Library)___ Chicago Lawn Branch, dedicated on December 1, 1960, serves the community.
The Chicago Lawn community area has supported the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ in the past two presidential elections.

In the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2016)___ , the Chicago Lawn cast 13,959 votes for ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ and cast 609 votes for ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ (93.87% to 4.10%).

In the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2012)___ , Chicago Lawn cast 15,171 votes for ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and cast 682 votes for ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ (95.24% to 4.28%).
